  "title": "Email confirmation | Linking a registered user to their existing guest checkout orders",
  "body": "**Who:** All users on the OFN\r\n**Trigger:** User confirms their email address\r\n**Goal:** To ensure that the enterprise can see the full order history for one email address (user), but protect the previous owner of the email address.\r\n\r\nFor epic #946, where any user at all has clicked on the 'confirm email address' link in the confirmation email they receive, the system must:\r\n- Check if the email address is associated with any guest checkout orders.\r\n- Where there have been previous guest checkout orders, the associated guest customer record must be linked to the newly registered user.\r\n- The guest order history does not show in the registered user's order history.\r\n- The enterprise can see the linkage between the guest orders and the subsequent registered user orders in their customer list.\r\n\r\nBackground on the design decision: Enterprises want to see the full order history of a customer. It doesn't matter if the customer was registered or not. It would also be very convenient to show all previous orders to the user. The problem is that we don't know which orders were really performed by the same person. We can't rely on the email address, because:\r\n\r\n- People misspell email addresses.\r\n- People change email addresses and email addresses change owners.\r\n- People invent email addresses for guest checkouts that actually exist.\r\n\r\nSo if we would show all guest orders with the same email address to the newly registered customer, they may see orders that don't belong to them. That breaches the privacy of the person that ordered as guest.\r\n\r\n-------\r\nSPIKE\r\n- How easy is this to implement? Will it work out of the box as @oeoeaio says?\r\n",
  "state": "closed",
  "closed_at": "2018-05-30T23:13:08Z",
  "updated_at": "2018-05-30T23:13:08Z"
}
